## Standards

## Standards review — target `5ae285b`

- **Must — hard violation — `test/native-session-sealer.test.ts:12,14`.** ADR 0016 says Pi’s natively enforced shape validation is not tested; tests must cover custom cross-field/branch logic only. These tests explicitly duplicate closed persisted-row formatting:
  > `"rejected lifecycle rows still require the direct closed Pi shape"`  
  > `"accepted issuance and result reject extra persisted fields"`
  
  Retain lifecycle distinctions (rejection→acceptance, missing vs invalid), but remove format-only extra-field oracles.

- **Should — judgement call — `src/recorder/session.ts`, `spawn.ts`, `manifest.ts`, `run.ts`, and associated tests. Mysterious Name.** Large production seams were compressed into dense single-line implementations with opaque names:
  > `const inode=(s:Identity)=>...`  
  > `function modified<T>(action:()=>T):T...`  
  > `const ds=modified(()=>lstatSync(owner.path))`  
  > `function outcome(s:...,diagnostic:...)`  
  > `function raw(root="/repo"):any`
  
  Names such as `s`, `ds`, `x`, `m`, `im`, `o`, and `c` obscure security-sensitive session identity, lifecycle, publication, and schema logic. Repo standards do not override this smell; use domain-revealing names and readable statement boundaries.

- **Should — judgement call — `src/recorder/extract.ts`. Duplicated Code.** Accepted and rejected lifecycle branches repeat the same persisted issuance/result closed-shape checks:
  > `if (!exact(issueRow,... ) || !exact(resultRow,... ) ... ) throw ...`
  
  followed later by near-identical `exact(resultRow...)` and `exact(issueRow...)` checks. Extract one lifecycle-pair shape validator, then layer accepted-only text/details validation on it.

Prior schema counterexamples are closed at this target: manifest receipt is required/non-null, failure schema now includes `session`/`directory` and omits stale `cleanup`; all three v2 schemas are closed with `additionalProperties:false`.

## Spec

## Spec review — target `5ae285bff7badc9ac102983bd43aec4decdc1b72`

- **Must — Native-session parsing remains effectively unbounded.** C3 requires “Stream JSONL” and C5 identifies “16 MiB JSONL line cap, finite entry cap, and **compact candidate state**” as the memory bounds. Instead, `readSession` retains every parsed object in `rows` (`src/recorder/session.ts:17-20`) before extraction. Up to 100,000 near-16-MiB entries can therefore exhaust memory. This contradicts the requested streaming/compact sealer design.

- **Must — Shipped manifest-v2 schema still permits an impossible successful manifest.** C7 says: “Manifest v2 requires a **non-null Receipt**” and “Remove … nullable successful-Receipt law.” Yet `schemas/recorder-manifest-v2.schema.json:172-176` explicitly accepts `receipt: null`. This also contradicts runtime success construction.

- **Must — Failure-v2 schema remains stale and incomplete.** C7 requires schemas to enumerate runtime “codes, stages, location segments,” while C6 requires honest cause preservation. The schema still allows obsolete diagnostic stage `"cleanup"` and omits runtime `"session"` (`schemas/recorder-failure-v2.schema.json:115-131`); its location enum omits config segments `"session"` and `"directory"` (`:64-91`). Runtime can emit those locations from config validation, so valid failures are rejected while stale shapes are public.

- **Should — Amended C8’s retained production-seam oracles are missing.** The amendment expressly retains: one counter-child invalid/valid invocation oracle; representative Recorder role integrations; derivative-redaction truth; exit, signal, and sealer-failure verticals; atomic publication/raw exclusion; runtime-object/schema synchronization; and cold-installed Recorder CLI smoke. Current Recorder tests only exercise parser/session leaf functions (`test/recorder-config-session-integrity.test.ts:1-23`) and extractor/forwarding leaves (`test/native-session-sealer.test.ts:1-15`); no test invokes `runRecorder`. `test/reviewer-package-lifecycle.test.ts:82-110` checks package inventory but not Recorder behavior or schema/runtime closure. Thus admission-before-spawn, injected argv/environment, publication, child-outcome honesty, promoted derivatives, and installed Recorder remain unproved under the thinned—not superseded—C8 requirements.

No substantive scope creep identified.

Summary: Standards — 3 findings (worst: hard ADR 0016 violation); Spec — 4 findings (worst: unbounded native-session parsing and public-schema contract failures).
